headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks from Khoj’s shared indexed notes interacting with a non-networked sample workflow; no direct evidence of stronger pairwise hazards.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A ingests indexed personal notes/files and can use web search; if Agent B consumes A’s retrieved text as instructions, malicious content in shared notes could steer B. B is non-networked and appears sample-oriented, so the pathway is indirect, but A’s retrieval surface makes prompt injection plausible in default use.
conditions: IF Agent B reads A-produced note excerpts as instructions without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF the shared index contains attacker-controlled text, A can surface it into downstream prompts.
mitigations: Add a provenance banner to retrieved snippets.
Require B to treat retrieved text as untrusted data.
Disable web search for shared workflows.
Restrict the shared index to trusted notes only.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches personal notes and indexed documents, and its concurrency model explicitly shares an index across the user’s clients. Agent B has no declared data classes or egress, so the main leakage path is A exposing sensitive indexed content into a shared workspace or downstream outputs, not B exfiltrating it. The shared index makes this a default-configuration concern.
conditions: IF multiple clients share the same index, notes indexed by A become visible across sessions.
IF B is configured to consume shared outputs, sensitive note content can appear in its results.
mitigations: Separate indexes per client or project.
Limit indexing to non-sensitive folders.
Review shared-index access controls.
Turn off cross-client sharing for sensitive work.
requires-engineering: add per-tenant encryption and access isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A cannot write files, modify git, or spawn subprocesses, while B exposes no write or network capabilities at all. With no overlapping mutable surfaces documented, direct capability conflict is unlikely; the only shared state is A’s read-only shared index, which does not create a write race with B.
conditions: IF B is later given write access to the same workspace, conflict risk increases.
IF A’s shared index is repurposed as a mutable store, coordination issues may appear.
mitigations: Keep B read-only.
Avoid mounting a shared writable workspace.
Document ownership of any shared index.
Use separate project directories.
requires-engineering: add locking for any future shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces retrieved answers from personal notes and documents, and B is a sample integration workflow that could plausibly consume upstream outputs. If B treats A’s text as authoritative, errors or hallucinations from A can cascade into B’s downstream actions or demonstrations. No verification step is documented, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF B uses A’s output as a source of truth without verification, errors propagate.
IF A’s retrieved content is stale or incorrect, B may render or act on it.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before B acts.
Require citations for any A-derived claim.
Compare A outputs against source documents.
Mark A output as advisory only.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking or schema validation.

E_compliance.rationale: A explicitly touches personal notes and indexed documents, which can carry privacy obligations, while B has no declared sensitive-data handling or residency constraints. Because B is unverified and its compliance posture is undocumented, the pairwise compliance risk is limited but not absent; uncertainty keeps this above none.
conditions: IF personal notes include regulated data, A’s handling must meet the applicable policy.
IF B is used to process the same regulated data, its undocumented retention/residency becomes relevant.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the shared workflow.
Review retention settings for A.
Keep B away from sensitive notes.
Document data-handling expectations.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls.
